title: pm: the low-risk arm reads the record's Security-touching line and the card's security label; absent is Tier H
body:
Fixes #33601

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9EjHJNDm9zkroCRfi1hziRF)_

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:低风险技能臂(技能措辞、只增的 ADR 注记可免人工批准落地)落地前多读两样:复核记录里一行 `Security-touching: no`,以及 PR 点名的每一张卡片(关闭关键字、`Part of`、`Refs` 指向的卡,和分支名对应的卡)有没有、或曾经有过 `security` 标签。缺行、读不出、不是 `no`、任一张卡带过该标签、另外点名的卡超过 8 张,一律回到 Tier H 等人批。
- **为什么改**:此前臂只看 PR 自身(路径、正文声明行、PR 上的标签),「这次改动教不教安全行为」没有人明文表态;现在由复核者在记录里明说,没说就按最严处理。
- **风险与回滚**:只收紧不放宽,最坏是本可免批的措辞 PR 多等一次人批。在途的臂 PR 需复核者重贴带该行的记录才回 Tier S。回滚即 revert 本 PR,无数据迁移。
- **先看**:① `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` 的 `lowRiskArmVerdict` 尾部(记录阶段)与 `readArmLanding`(事后巡检只对带规则的落地套用);② `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` 的 `readLowRiskRecordStage` 与 `readCardLabels`;③ `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` 的 `contractReviewRecordReading`。
- **两分钟验证**:`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template`,预期模板里 `Scope:` 的下一行是 `Security-touching: yes`(不改就粘贴即按最严处理)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位达档复核后落地。

## What changes

The low-risk skills arm (`lowRiskArmVerdict`) gains a **record stage**, read last and only when every pull-read condition already holds. It is two conjuncts:

1. the contract-review record of record on this head carries exactly one bare `Security-touching: no` line. The line reads when it is bare, behind a list bullet, in bold, or with its value alone in a code span. An absent line, an unreadable one and `yes` are each Tier H with the reason printed. Unreadable shapes: two lines, a quoted line, a fenced or code-indented line, the key inside a code span (the spelling prose uses to mention the line), trailing words, any other value, a near-miss key;
2. no card the PR names carries the `security` label or ever had it removed (each card's labels and its timeline). The cards a PR names are every closing-keyword target, every `Part of` target, every `Refs` target and the card its branch is named for. A PR that names no card, a card that could not be read, a reading that does not say it read the other cards, and a PR that names more than eight cards beyond the first are each Tier H; past that limit nothing more is read.

The verdict now says how far the stage got (`recordStage`: `not-reached`, `pending`, `read`). A reading that hands in no stage never answers Tier S: with every pull-read condition holding it reads Tier H on one reason, `pending`, and the caller reads the stage and asks again. No stand-in read answers the stage.

By file:

- `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`: `contractReviewRecordReading` returns `securityTouching` (`missing`, `read` with `no` or `yes`, or `unreadable` with its reason), beside the existing recognisers. The key and its two values are exported once.
- `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`: `--template` prints `Security-touching: yes` under `Scope:` (an unedited paste fails closed), the legend says when `no` may be written, and the review brief hands the reviewer the line. It re-exports the reader's key and values. `namedCardNumbers` lists every card a pull request names.
- `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` (the register): the stage in `lowRiskArmVerdict`, judged over the first card and every other named card; `--pr` reads it through `pullRecordStage`; the post-merge sweep reads it in `readArmLanding`, with each card's labels rebuilt as they stood at the landing (`cardLabelsAsLanded`), and only for a landing whose own tree carries the stage (`armRecordStageBound`).
- `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: one reader for every site, `readLowRiskRecordStage` (threads through `readRecordThreads`, the line through `lowRiskRecordStage`, the cards through `readCardLabels` and `makeLabelReader`). `readCardLabels` reads the first card as before and every other named card under `others`, up to `LOW_RISK_NAMED_CARD_LIMIT` (8). The queue leg reads the stage for an arm entry nothing else cleared. `makeTimelineReader` now follows the `Link` header past a short page.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` (the relay): `lowRiskReadingFor` reads the stage before `governedReviewPlan` decides to request nobody, so `pr_ready` on an arm PR whose record lacks the line, or that names a labelled card, requests the approvers as for any Tier H pull request.
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md`: one line now names the `Security-touching:` line next to the independence pair and points at `--template` for the values. Same line count (63), same file family. The words that line gave up are the two key spellings `Implemented-by:` and `Reviewed-by:`, which stay spelled in `references/lanes/review.md` and in the `--template` output.

Where the arm is read, and what each site answers:

| Site | Reader | An arm PR whose record lacks the line | An arm PR that names a second card carrying `security` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| queue guard | `readLowRiskTier` with the stage from `readLowRiskRecordStage` | Tier H: the entry is refused unless an authorized approval or enqueue cleared it | the same |
| relay, on `pr_ready` | `lowRiskReadingFor` | Tier H: the approvers are requested | the same |
| `--pr N` | `pullRecordStage` | Tier H with the reason | Tier H, both cards read |
| post-merge sweep | `readArmLanding` | BREACH on the record stage, for a landing whose tree carries the stage | BREACH when the label stood at the landing; a label added afterwards is not one |

At the sweep, a landing that names more cards than the leg reads is a stage BREACH (the queue counted the same names and refused it), and another named card that cannot be read is NOT MEASURED.

## Why

The arm lands a pull request with no human approval, on what the pull request itself shows: its paths, its body's declaration lines, its labels and its changesets. Whether the change teaches security behaviour was nobody's written statement: the seat was expected to add the `security` label, and a forgotten label read as clean. The record is the one artefact a reviewer at the review tier writes on the head, so the statement belongs there, and its absence has to read as the strictest answer. The card's label is read as well, as the card asks: a label put on the card is not inherited by a pull request opened later. Every named card is read, not only the one the delivery relation ranks first, because a `Part of` card beside a closing-keyword card, or the card a branch is named for, can carry the label too.

## Tests

Self-tests on the head `13c0c84ffe4f15a9fd50d8588c46f61f9f122c6c`, all exit 0:

| File | Result | Battery floors moved by this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `check-half-states.mjs` | 5293 cases | `H43 hand-off timing` 88 to 103 (94 for this PR's rows, then 103 for the nine verdict-reader rows `main` added with no pin; the battery registers 126) |
| `record-recognisers.mjs` | 430 cases | template 32 to 38, thread set 19 to 22, letter-C scope 22 to 24 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` | 581 cases | arm at the queue 54 to 84, ADR leg at the queue 12 to 14, enqueue leg 28 to 30 |
| `check-governed-merges.mjs` | 908 assertions | arm 74 to 100, sweep 51 to 71 |
| `fleet-write/execute.mjs` | 424 cases, 30 batteries | governed review 45 to 52 |

### Forced test edits (named)

Each of these rows pinned Tier S, a reading shape or a wording that this PR changes by design.

- `check-half-states.mjs`:
  - the row that pins the template record's whole reading as JSON (`… the template record reads one PASS, no FAIL, no grade`) gains `"securityTouching":{"state":"missing"}`.
  - the row for the one bare line read behind a bullet, in bold or in a code span now says the VALUE alone may sit in a span; its whole-line-in-a-span sample moved to the new unreadable row.
- `record-recognisers.mjs`: the template-legend row expects the legend's new wording.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`:
  - `⛔ CONTROL: the-same-skills-PR-with-NO-record-is-REFUSED-Tier-S-without-its-record` is now `…-REFUSED-Tier-H-on-the-record-stage`: with no record the arm itself reads Tier H.
  - `⛔ a-record-on-an-OLDER-head-is-REFUSED` is now `…-REFUSED-Tier-H-its-line-does-not-carry-forward`.
  - `⛔ a-recogniser-set-without-the-verdict-reader-REFUSES-the-arm-fail-closed` is now `⛔ a-recogniser-set-without-the-record-reader-REFUSES-fail-closed-the-arm-at-Tier-H-every-other-Tier-S-leg-on-its-verdict`.
  - the two `⛔ SF1-a-record-carried-over-a-hop-…` rows (rewritten changeset, moved catalog text) keep their names and are re-pinned to Tier H with no record read.
  - `⛔ CONTROL: the-same-ADR-note-with-NO-record-is-REFUSED-Tier-S-without-its-record` is now `…-REFUSED-Tier-H-on-the-record-stage`.
  - the arm fixtures' records carry `Security-touching: no`.
  - `readCardLabels-never-throws-and-counts-its-reads-a-card-nobody-could-name-reads-nothing` hands in the named cards and its reading gains `others`; `readLowRiskRecordStage-derives-the-card-…` gains `others` in its card reading.
- `check-governed-merges.mjs`:
  - `⭐ --pr-carries-the-arm-reading-…-it-answers-Tier-S` is now `…-its-record-stage-is-PENDING-at-Tier-H`.
  - both arm fixtures hand in a favourable record stage with an empty measured `others`; the sweep fixture's record carries the line, its readers answer the cards' labels and timelines, and its git answers the landed tree's copy of the register.
  - `the-Tier-S-words-name-the-record-line-and-the-card` expects "the PR or a card it names".
- `fleet-write/execute.mjs`: `⭐ low-risk-skills-pull-requests-no-one` also pins the four stage reads on the relay's token; its fixture answers them, and its card reading gains `others`.

The merge of `main` forced no test edit: its one conflict was between two sets of added rows in the `H43` battery, and both sets are kept.

## Acceptance notes

Behaviour a reviewer should judge, each chosen toward Tier H:

- The template ships `Security-touching: yes`, so a record pasted without editing the line fails closed.
- Each named card's timeline is read as well as its labels: a `security` label that was ever removed from a card keeps Tier H. This goes one step past the card's wording (the label on the linked card) and mirrors what the arm already does for the PR's own label.
- Every card the PR names is read, which is wider than the cards it delivers: a `Refs` target and the card a branch is named for count. The card whose thread may carry the record is still the one the delivery relation answers, and no other named card is searched for a record.
- A PR that names no card reads Tier H on the arm, and so does one that names more than eight cards beyond the first.
- The cards are the ones the PR body names when the leg reads it, at the queue and again at the sweep. An edit to the body after the review changes which cards are read; that is the same trust the PASS record itself stands on, and the conjunct is not tamper-proof.
- The line reader does not judge how GitHub renders the record. A bare line inside an HTML comment, inside a `pre` element, after a code span opened on an earlier line, or directly under a quoted line still reads. Only an author the guard trusts can write a record.
- An arm entry whose record thread cannot be read refuses as Tier H.
- The stage is never read for an entry the maintainer cleared, and its outcome is unchanged. An entry an authorized enqueue cleared prints Tier H with the pending reason. An entry an approval cleared stops one conjunct earlier, on the timeline the leg never read.
- In-flight arm pull requests return to Tier S only when their record is posted again with the line. No record written before this change carries it.
- The sweep applies the stage only to a landing whose own tree declares it. The queue leg runs the register from the merge group's tree, so an earlier landing was judged without the stage and stays a pass on its record alone, with a note in its row. A landed tree that cannot be read is NOT MEASURED.
- The timeline reader ends its walk on a short page only when the answer's `Link` header names no next page. Whether the timeline route ever answers a short page that is not the last was not measured; the header settles it either way. The comment, review and label readers keep the short-page rule.
- Cost: for an arm entry that reaches the stage the queue leg spends two more reads per named card (its labels and its timeline); the relay spends two thread reads and two per named card on `pr_ready`. `GET /repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/N/labels` accepts `pull_requests=read`, so no workflow permission moves.

Outside this card's file surface, noted and not changed:

- `AGENTS.md`, the register's parenthetical naming `lowRiskArmVerdict`, still says only that the seat labels unnamed security teaching. It does not mention the record stage.
- `.github/workflows/fleet-patrols.yml`, the sweep job's comment, still defines a BREACH as an arm landing without a same-head at-tier PASS record. A record stage at Tier H is now a BREACH too.
- Both are carried by a comment on card #33768.
- In `armSettledWithoutUnread` the disjunct `guard.landsOnLowRiskArm(work)` can no longer be true on a first read. It is left in place: this PR adds one condition on that line and does not touch `favourableArmGitRead` next to it, which another card in flight is editing. Whichever lands second merges the neighbouring line.

## Verification

Local gates, derived on the head `13c0c84ffe4f15a9fd50d8588c46f61f9f122c6c` with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` and run one by one, each exit code captured before any pipe:

- 76 derived, 76 run. On the first pass 75 exit 0 and `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` exits 3, prerequisite not met: the workspace CLI was not built. After that gate's own one-command build closure under the verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`) it exits 0. `--ran` on the final record answers `76 derived, 76 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. The list was 64 commands until `main` taught the deriver to follow the import graph of `scripts/pm`; those 64 ran too, every one exit 0, on the head before the third merge.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` needs `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` built. They were built under the verify lock in round 1; the merges since changed neither package's source.
- `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet` and `pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint` are in the list and exit 0: `references/contract-review.md` stays at 63 lines.
- Outside the derived list, run by hand: `node scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD`, exit 0 on 11 commit messages. `pnpm check:adr-anchors` is in the derived list now.
- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34133` on the pushed head reads GOVERNED, Tier S, through its one `.claude/**` path; the five `scripts/pm` files are not on the register.
- Changed lines against `main`: 1709 (+1577 / -132) over 6 files, under the 3000-line human-merge line.
- `main` was merged in three times. The second merge (`86350e12`) had one conflict, in the self-test of `check-half-states.mjs`; the reader itself merged cleanly, and the five self-tests, the ablations that touch the reader and the 64 gates derived then ran after it, all exit 0. The third merge (`b4eea885`, fetched right before the push) had no conflict; the five self-tests and the gate list above ran on it.

The families only CI runs (the type-check lanes, the Test Core shards, the artifact rosters) are left to this PR's check runs.
